tip: That comma inside ό,τι (o,ti) is part of the word: ό,τι = whatever. Without it, ότι (oti) means 'that'. Here ό,τι κάνει (o,ti kani) = whatever makes.
The raised dot after παρακινεί (parakini) is the ano teleia – Greek's semicolon. The ; symbol has a different job in Greek: it is the question mark.
Αφενός (afenos)... αφετέρου (afeterou) is a fixed pair – literally 'from one side... from the other side'. When you see αφενός, expect αφετέρου later in the sentence.
Εν κατακλείδι (en katakleidi) = in conclusion. Εν is ancient 'in' plus a dative case modern Greek has lost – it survives only in frozen phrases like this.
Δεδομένου ότι (dedomenou oti) = given that – literally 'of it being given', a frozen ancient genitive. Treat the whole phrase as one chunk meaning 'since'.
